seoTitle: Transfer a Domain from GoDaddy to Namecheap
metaDescription: Moving your domain from GoDaddy to Namecheap? Learn how to unlock it, get the EPP/Auth code, and complete the transfer step by step.
intro: Moving a domain from GoDaddy to Namecheap can make sense for better pricing, cleaner privacy protection, or just having everything under one registrar, and the process itself is a five-step checklist rather than anything technical. The two things that trip people up are unlocking the domain before starting and getting the authorization code to the right place — everything else is filling in a form and waiting. This guide follows the actual screens on both sides: GoDaddy's transfer-out checklist and Namecheap's transfer intake.

steps.heading: Start the transfer-out process in GoDaddy
steps.body: Log in to GoDaddy and go to Domains > Domain Portfolio, then find the domain and choose Domain Transfer Out. GoDaddy shows a banner first suggesting you may not need a full transfer if you're only trying to connect the domain to a third-party service — that's a different, simpler process. If you genuinely want to move the domain's registration, dismiss that banner and read the five-item transfer checklist GoDaddy lays out: confirm your admin contact email is current, verify the new registrar will set up DNS, start the transfer at the new registrar, authorize it with the code GoDaddy emails you, and expect confirmation within 5-7 days.

image.caption: GoDaddy's Domain Transfer Out checklist, spelling out the five steps from confirming contact info to the 5-7 day completion window.

steps.heading: Unlock the domain and get its authorization code
steps.body: Click Continue with transfer, and GoDaddy walks you to the registrar lock setting — domains are locked by default specifically to block unauthorized transfers, so it has to be switched off before Namecheap can pull it. Once unlocked, request the EPP or Auth code; GoDaddy emails it to the administrative contact address on file, so this is the moment that email address needs to be one you can actually access right now.

steps.heading: Find the domain in your Namecheap account
steps.body: Log in to Namecheap and go to Domain List from the left sidebar, which shows every domain already in your account along with its status, auto-renew setting, and expiration date. This is also where the transferred domain will eventually land once the process completes, so it's worth knowing your way around this screen before you kick off the transfer.

image.caption: The Namecheap Domain List, showing existing domains with their status and expiration — the same screen your transferred domain will appear on once it completes.

steps.heading: Enter the domain and the authorization code
steps.body: Start a new transfer through Namecheap's Transfer to Us flow and enter the domain name. Namecheap's transfer checklist confirms the current registrar (GoDaddy.com, LLC in this case) and shows the registrar lock status — it needs to read 'Unlocked' here, matching the step you just completed on GoDaddy's side, with a Refresh button if it still shows locked. Paste the authorization code GoDaddy emailed you into the Authorization Code field and click Verify Auth Code before moving on.

image.caption: Namecheap's transfer checklist, confirming GoDaddy as the current registrar and an unlocked domain, with a field for the authorization code.

steps.heading: Add the transfer to your cart and confirm the order
steps.body: Once the auth code verifies, add the domain transfer to your cart alongside any other items — privacy protection is commonly included free, and you'll see options like SSL certificates offered as add-ons you can skip if you don't need them. Review the subtotal, apply a promo code if you have one, and click Confirm Order. This purchase is what actually pays for and initiates the transfer on Namecheap's end; nothing moves until this order is placed.

image.caption: The Namecheap checkout cart with the domain transfer line item and its authorization code attached, ready to confirm.

steps.heading: Approve the transfer by email and wait it out
steps.body: After confirming the order, watch your inbox for a confirmation email — Namecheap sends this to verify you actually requested the transfer, and GoDaddy may send its own notification too, since both registrars want confirmation before letting a domain change hands. Approve it, then check the transfer status periodically inside Namecheap's Domain List. Most transfers complete within the 5-7 day window GoDaddy quoted on the checklist, though ICANN's mandatory hold period means it's rarely faster than about 5 days even when everything goes smoothly.

faq.question: Do I need to unlock my domain before transferring?
faq.answer: Yes. GoDaddy locks domains by default to prevent unauthorized transfers, and Namecheap's own transfer checklist checks the lock status and won't proceed until it reads Unlocked.

faq.question: What is an EPP/Auth code used for?
faq.answer: It's a security code from your current registrar that proves domain ownership. Namecheap's transfer form has a dedicated Authorization Code field and a Verify Auth Code button to confirm it before you can add the transfer to your cart.

faq.question: How long does a domain transfer take?
faq.answer: GoDaddy's own checklist quotes 5-7 days for confirmation, and ICANN's mandatory hold period means it's rarely much faster than about 5 days even when the code and lock status are correct on the first try.

faq.question: Will my website go down during the transfer?
faq.answer: Typically no, since DNS settings and hosting usually remain unaffected during a standard registrar transfer — you're changing who administers the domain, not where it points.

faq.question: What if GoDaddy shows a banner saying I don't need to transfer?
faq.answer: That banner refers to connecting your domain to a third-party service, which is a separate, simpler DNS change. If your goal is to actually move the domain's registration to Namecheap, dismiss it and continue with the transfer checklist.
